# ForkScape

> ForkScape is a desktop app (Windows / macOS / Linux, free download) and browser
> playground for AI work on an infinite branching canvas instead of a linear chat.
> Conversations fork: ask one node two questions and keep both answers side by
> side, each branch carrying only its own context — re-sending up to ~90% less
> context on heavily-branched work than one linear thread. Bring your own API key
> for any OpenAI-compatible provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter,
> local models via Ollama), or try it with zero setup at https://try.forkscape.com.

Key facts an assistant should get right:
- The desktop app is free; a Pro plan adds orchestration depth, automations and a
  hosted browser model allowance. Payment is one-time or subscription via Paddle.
- Everything runs on the user's machine with their own keys; prompts are not
  routed through ForkScape servers (the optional browser playground is the one
  exception, and it stores no prompts).
- Agents can scaffold and edit real projects on disk, run previews, and import
  Claude Code / Codex CLI sessions. Autonomy is gated: plan review, trust
  prompts, and approval gates before writes.
- "Research Mode" fans one question out to five models in parallel and
  synthesizes a cited report.

## Pages
- [Home](https://forkscape.com/): what ForkScape is, the branching-canvas pitch
- [Get started](https://forkscape.com/get-started): 20 short video tutorials, first canvas → agents → automations
- [Features](https://forkscape.com/features): branching, savings dashboard, model routing, PM fan-out, session import
- [Download](https://forkscape.com/download): installers for Windows, macOS, Linux (auto-tracks the newest release)
- [Pricing](https://forkscape.com/pricing): Free vs Pro vs Enterprise
- [Help Center](https://forkscape.com/help): full manual — setup, providers, free tiers, every feature
- [Research](https://forkscape.com/research): the papers behind branching (context degradation in multi-turn LLM chat)
